responsibilities: Lead the development of data models to consume, transform, and expose data to stakeholders and systems across the company
Collect business requirements, define successful analytics outcomes, and design data solutions
Set company-wide standards for data regarding structure, quality, and expectations
Contribute Flex’s data culture by influencing processes, systems, and tools that enable to make better decisions in a scalable way

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Strong perspective on analytics engineering development cycle (data modeling, version control, documentation + testing, and best practices for codebase development and CI/CD)
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour: engineering-discipline language dominates — 'version control, documentation + testing, and best practices for codebase development and CI/CD' plus 'Set company-wide standards for data regarding structure, quality'.
evidence.domain_risk: Flex is a growth-stage, NYC headquartered FinTech company that is creating the best rent payment experience.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: High: this is a fintech handling consumers' rent payments, and the JD requires 'Experience within the fintech space' outright.
evidence.data_team_maturity: As part of the broader Data team, you will report to the Director, Analytics Engineering and support a number of different areas across Flex.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mature: analytics engineering is a named sub-team inside 'the broader Data team' with its own Director, and Snowflake, dbt and BI tooling are already in place.
evidence.jd_authorship: Set company-wide standards for data regarding structure, quality, and expectations
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Mixed: the scope is genuinely specific ('Set company-wide standards for data') but no responsibility bullet names a tool, system or volume — the stack detail sits in the requirements instead.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: you will enable stakeholders at Flex to easily find the data they need to make decisions
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: internal_data: the deliverable is a modelling layer other data people consume — 'expose data to stakeholders and systems across the company', with analysts, engineers and PMs as the named partners.
evidence.autonomy_level: Set company-wide standards for data regarding structure, quality, and expectations
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic: the verbs are direction-setting — 'Lead the development', 'Set company-wide standards', 'define successful analytics outcomes', 'influencing processes, systems, and tools'.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: None: no AI, LLM or AI-tooling language appears anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Set company-wide standards for data regarding structure, quality, and expectations
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility: quality standards are something the role sets for the whole company, with testing named again in the development-cycle requirement.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Set company-wide standards for data regarding structure, quality, and expectations
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: quality governance is one of four responsibilities, framed as enablement and standard-setting rather than as guarding against regulatory exposure or bad numbers reaching decision-makers.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Lead the development of data models to consume, transform, and expose data to stakeholders and systems across the company
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Greenfield: every responsibility verb is constructive — 'Lead the development', 'design data solutions', 'Set company-wide standards' — with no remediation or migration work named.
evidence.work_arrangement: This is a hybrid position with on-site expectations of 3 days per week in our New York Headquarters.
evidence.loss_aversion: Risk framing is limited to standard-setting: 'Set company-wide standards for data regarding structure, quality, and expectations', with no incident, compliance or trust language.
